title: Owner can frontrun a pending batchMint by changing nudgePaymentToken, denying the user their incentive
description: The setters apply immediately with no timelock or two-step. An owner who sees a pending high-`count` `batchMint` in the mempool can frontrun it by (a) raising `nudgeSize` above the user's `count`, (b) zeroing `nudgePaymentToken`, or (c) changing `nudgePaymentToken` to match the user's `paymentToken` — which forces a revert and traps the user's intent. Conversely, the owner can also drain the contract's nudge balance by calling `setNudgePaymentToken(otherToken)` then sweeping with their own batch.
exploit_scenario: 1) Alice broadcasts a 1000-unit `batchMint` qualifying for a nudge worth 10,000 USDC. 2) Owner front-runs with `setNudgeSize(2000)`. 3) Alice's tx executes — `count (1000) >= nudgeSize (2000)` is false, so no nudge is paid. 4) Owner calls `setNudgeSize(100)` again and pockets the next batch (their own).
recommended_mitigation: Add a timelock or 2-step accept pattern on both `setNudgeSize` and `setNudgePaymentToken`, or document this as an accepted centralization risk. At minimum emit a queued-change event some blocks before the change takes effect so users can re-route.
notes: Centralization concern. Per project's CLAUDE.md, owner privileges are accepted; flagging as low/QA. Phoenix accepts admin privileges as documented, so this is informational.
